description: A waste, with a crowd in it

participation.context: Heard the waste, refused Daniel, and did not argue the crowd on the shop floor.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Said the lecture in the shop, with you, and kept the book for the stair.
participation.name: Richard Field

participation.context: Moved the wet quire, and took the candle up without the lecture.
participation.name: Jacqueline Field

relations.quote: Plays are a waste. A waste with a crowd in it.

story.body: You asked for a chronicle and got the shop first. Field said plays are a waste, and a waste with a crowd, and he said it to you. You left Daniel unbought. You agreed the book was a loan before you had lifted it, and you went up without a speech in defence of a playhouse.

relations.quote: Plays are a waste. A waste with a crowd in it.

title: Heard Field call plays a waste

participation.context: Read four columns on your feet, named no return day, and carried the book.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Spoke thou, lent the volume, and kept the gap as his morning fact.
participation.name: Richard Field

participation.context: Set the stool, and then set the quires in the place where you stood.
participation.name: Jacqueline Field

relations.quote: I'll see the gap on that shelf every morning till it's home.

relations.note: the visit ended by the quires
relations.quote: These quires go where your feet are.

story.body: You opened the second volume standing, and it fell at the second Richard. You read four columns without sitting, and you did not begin a speech. Jacqueline ended the visit by putting the afternoon's quires where you were standing. You took the book in both arms and carried it home through Cheapside.

relations.quote: I'll see the gap on that shelf every morning till it's home.

relations.note: the visit ended by the quires
relations.quote: These quires go where your feet are.

title: Read four columns and carried the book

participation.context: Closed the poem and left the new leaf empty for a moment.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

relations.note: the loan is in the room and still his

story.body: You shut Brooke on the blank days and wrote that no speech had gone in. The chronicle was in the room and was not yet the page you meant to head.

relations.note: the loan is in the room and still his

participation.context: Wrote the shape, copied without speaking, and stopped before a line anyone could say.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

relations.note: the book is the source of the shape, and still his

story.body: You dated the new heading and set five lines on a folded sheet. You copied the heralds as a copyist's act and did not turn the copy into a speech. You wrote that Verona is shut and that there is no speech.

relations.note: the book is the source of the shape, and still his

topics: the heralds copied and not spoken
